name: Chris Coons

issue_poll.name: AP VoteCast Delaware, Oct 26–Nov 3, 2020; plus Pew Research Center, July 27–Aug 2, 2020
issue_poll.note: Ranks 1–5 from AP VoteCast Delaware most-important-issue question (coronavirus 44%, economy 25%, racism 9%, health care 8%, immigration 4%); only these five were published. Ranks 6–10 from national Pew 'very important' shares not already covered (Supreme Court appointments 64%, violent crime 59%, foreign policy 57%, gun policy 55%, economic inequality 49%): https://www.pewresearch.org/politics/2020/08/13/important-issues-in-the-2020-election/

issues.position: More COVID relief, including aid to state and local governments
Invest in infrastructure to rebuild the economy after the pandemic
Pass the Justice in Policing Act
issues.note: George Floyd Justice in Policing Act never received a Senate floor vote this term.

issues.position: Strengthen the ACA with a public option; lower drug prices

votes.bill_title: Inflation Reduction Act (drug price negotiation, ACA subsidies)
votes.question: On passage

issues.note: A public option never received a floor vote; rated on ACA subsidies and drug pricing.

issues.position: Pass the Dream and Promise Act; bipartisan immigration reform
issues.note: No Senate floor vote on Dreamer legalization or comprehensive reform this term.

issues.position: Opposed Barrett confirmation (before term); open-minded on Court expansion
Opposes defunding police; backs community policing (general)
Require congressional approval for military force against Iran
Strengthen background checks for gun purchases

votes.question: On the motion to concur in the House amendment with an amendment

issues.note: Universal checks never got a floor vote; BSCA expanded checks for buyers under 21.

issues.position: Expand the Child Tax Credit and EITC

caveats: Delaware poll published only five issues; ranks 6–10 use national Pew data.
Iran war powers votes inferred from tallies (47-53, Fetterman the only Democrat opposed); roll call numbers for those and for H.R.2938 not confirmed.
No 2020 pledge on a $15 minimum wage found; he voted against the Sanders $15 amendment to H.R.1319 (Mar 2021), which is not scored.
Economic inequality position comes from an April 2020 Senate letter he signed, not a campaign statement.
